cards.body:
## Summary
The dossier's three AUTO repairs fire on id lists the sheet already carries (phoneIds, ids, staleIds), but no read tool exposes them, so an agent can only repair what happens to be in a table's six sample rows. Derive one remedy plan per table in the model, have the dossier's buttons and the agent's reads both take their arguments from it, and add a read-only plan_repairs tool that pages it.

## Description
The parity seam: the person and the agent act on the same server actions, but the person's arguments are built inline in Gate.tsx from BkTable fields and the agent's must be scraped from samples. Measured on a scratch seed (2026-10-25, 46 tables): 120 rows have a malformed phone and 100 of them appear in any read; 135 rows are stale and unflagged and only 68 appear (50%); 14 of 45 tables with phone work have targets the agent cannot see. The journey's normalise beat works around it by previewing whatever the first 25 sampled rows are.

model/remedies.ts is pure and client-safe: remediesOf(table) -> Remedy[] where each rule-repairable kind carries {preview, act} as tool name plus arguments, batched at MAX_IDS (lib/constants), and the person-only kind (duplicate) carries pair ids and by:'person' with no act at all (hitl-approval/oracle-before-gate: the preview is named before the act; the distinction read.ts exists to protect is kept). dossierRead adds remedies; plan_repairs {database?, kind?, page?} returns remedies across tables through the kit's boundedPage, read-only, description under the 240-char cap (ADR 0070). Gate.tsx's three handlers read the same module, so the button and the agent cannot drift (mcp-tools/tool-schema-design, one-authority-per-vocabulary).

Not a policy change: normalize_fields and flag_stale stay AUTO, merge and delete stay GATED and are never named by a remedy; the agent gains opaque contact ids, fewer fields than the names, emails and phones dossierRead already sends.

## Flow
- agent: plan_repairs {kind:'stale'} -> pages of {table, database, act:{tool:'flag_stale', args:{ids}}}
- agent proposes flag_stale with exactly those ids; the host classes it AUTO as today
- person in the dossier: Flag N stale rows fires remediesOf(table).stale.act.args - the same list
- duplicates: remedy says by:'person' and lists pair ids for read_pairs/preview_merge; nothing to call

## Expected impact
An agent can carry out every repair the dossier offers, on every target, in one read per page instead of 46 open_item+read_view pairs that still miss half the stale rows. The journey's normalise beat can preview the real phone targets.

## Evaluation
Claim: every act target a dossier button fires on is reachable by a read, and both derive from one module
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (module and tool absent); 68 of 135 stale targets and 100 of 120 phone targets visible to any read
After: 8 of 8; 135 of 135 and 120 of 120
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: Walk the sheet worst-first from inside the dossier, across databases, in one key
shared_surfaces: examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/Dossier.tsx and Blocks.tsx (owned by tidycrm-blocks-ui, not in r3: an onStep prop, a position line and two keys; ~60 lines)
acceptance: worklistOf(sheet) on the scratch seed -> excludes every table with deviationTotal 0 and attention false; its length equals the count of the rest; entry 0 is searchBlocks(sheet, {}).items[0]
worklistOf(sheet) order -> for every adjacent pair: attention before not, then deviationTotal descending, then ident ascending (a total, deterministic order)
stepWorklist(list, null, 'next') -> {group: list[0].database, item: list[0].ident, at: 1, of: list.length}
stepWorklist(list, {ident: list[k].ident, at: k+1}, 'next') where list[k+1] lives in another database -> {group: list[k+1].database, item: list[k+1].ident, at: k+2}
stepWorklist from the last entry with 'next', and from the first with 'previous' -> null (no wrap; the surface says the end was reached)

stepWorklist(listWithoutK, {ident: list[k].ident, at: k+1}, 'next') - the current table was cleared by a write and the refreshed list no longer holds it -> the entry that slid into its place (old list[k+1]), not the head of the list

runTool(next_table, {direction:'next'}) at L2 on the worst table -> the nav's openItem is reached once with (list[1].database, list[1].ident); result carries at 2, of N, the table's tableRead and arrives_in_ms = ARRIVAL_MS; at L0 it opens list[0]
guard: searchBlocks(sheet, {}) returns the same ids in the same order after worstFirst moves from tools/search.ts into model/worklist.ts
premise: examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/sheet/Head.tsx:41 - the head prints 'deviations outstanding' and (:47) 'pairs awaiting a person' as figures with no way to go to them
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/tools/search.ts:57 - worstFirst, the order 'a person is waiting on, then the most deviations', exists only behind the agent's search_blocks
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/Blocks.tsx:314 - the dossier gets onClose={nav.up} and nothing else; Blocks.tsx:256 opens a table only from a card inside the current database
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/beats.ts:99 - each database change costs ARRIVAL_MS (1,120 ms) of flight and dress before its cards can be read and clicked
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/l0/cells.ts:24 - 43 of 46 tables touch an open pair, so the L0 colour cannot tell a reader which table to open next
cards.rollback: Two commits (worklist module + search.ts reuse + next_table tool + tests; Dossier/Blocks wiring). Revert the surface commit alone to keep the tool, or both; search_blocks' order is pinned by the guard case either way.

cards.body:
## Summary
A person clearing the sheet works one table at a time, but the dossier can only be closed: the next-worst table is usually in another database, behind an Escape, a database jump with its 1.1 s flight and dress, and a visual search among five or six cards. Put the worst-first order in the model as a worklist, give the dossier next/previous (two keys and a 'next worst - 4 of 43' line), and give the agent the same walk as next_table.

## Description
The order already exists - search_blocks sorts 'the tables a person is waiting on, then the most outstanding deviations' - but only an agent can reach it, and it is a private comparator inside tools/search.ts. model/worklist.ts takes it over (search.ts imports it, so the two cannot disagree) and adds a total tie-break on ident (table/sorting: deterministic order). stepWorklist(list, from, dir) is pure: it returns the next focus {group, item, at, of}, crosses databases freely, does not wrap, and when the table just repaired has left the refreshed list it continues from the slot it held rather than jumping to the head (hitl-approval/review-queues: the pending set from the system of record, enough context to decide in place). The dossier's step calls nav.openItem(group, item); when the group changes the camera flies under the card exactly as an agent's open_item does today, and useArrival stages that flight as it already does for any group change. next_table is read-and-move like open_item: readOnlyHint, no consequentialHint, description under 240 chars.

## Flow
- person opens the worst table (or presses the head's first step from L0)
- repairs it in the dossier; the server refresh drops it from the list
- presses ] : the camera flies to the next database under the card, the card re-keys to the next table, the line reads '2 of 42'
- [ goes back; at the end the line says the list is done
- agent: next_table {direction:'next'} -> the same focus and position, one call instead of search_blocks + open_item

## Expected impact
One key per table instead of four acts and a visual search per table, across 43 tables; a person always knows how much is left. The agent's walk and the person's walk are the same list.

## Evaluation
Claim: the next table worth a person's attention is one step from any dossier, ordered by the rule search_blocks already uses
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard acceptance cases pass (no worklist module, no next_table)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
